subject: Urgent: FinPay production 5xx/429 spike — possible retry storm
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, FinPay SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>
Cc: Devon Lee <devon@finpay.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:14:00 +0000
Subject: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike affecting checkout — need urgent help

Connor —

We started seeing elevated 5xx/429 rates and timeouts on our live checkout between ~08:50-09:10 UTC. Error rates peaked at ~18% for token-generation calls to your API and correlated with a surge in client retries. Our stack trace suggests a lot of parallel retries originating from our payment-worker fleet. This is causing timeouts and visible latency for customers.

Attached: error_logs_20260221.txt (trimmed), screenshot_429.png showing dashboard.

Can you confirm whether there were any known platform issues or rollouts in that window? If not, we suspect a retry storm on our side but would appreciate any quick triage/mitigation advice while we investigate.

Asha Rao
SRE Lead, FinPay
asha@finpay.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike affecting checkout — need urgent help

Thanks Asha — we're looking into it now. No planned rollouts or infra changes on our side during that window. I'm looping in Evelyn (Customer Success) and Vivek (SRE/Platform) to help triage.

Immediate asks while we triage:
- Can you share the time-aligned client config (retries/backoff) if possible?
- Is the spike still ongoing for you or did it subside?

We will escalate if we see any platform anomalies.

—Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>, FinPay SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Escalation: FinPay 5xx/429 spike — gathering logs + action plan

Team —

I'm escalating this to Platform and creating an action list. Connor, thanks for the heads up. Vivek, can you validate server-side metrics and check for request floods or KV cache evictions around 08:50-09:10 UTC?

Asha, attached are the logs you sent; I've also pulled platform ingress metrics and a short traceroute (see related_links).

Immediate mitigation suggestions while we dig deeper:
- Rate-limit: add a conservative client-side in-flight cap (max_concurrent_requests=5)
- Respect server Retry-After headers and honor HTTP 429 backoff windows
- Temporary throttle on non-critical background workers

We'll update within 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>, FinPay SRE Team <sre@finpay.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Escalation: FinPay 5xx/429 spike — preliminary analysis

Asha / team —

Prelim findings from platform side: no code deploys or capacity-reduction events during the window. However, we see a sharp inbound request fan-in from a small set of FinPay IP ranges with very low client-side backoffs. Key observations:

- Error pattern: mix of 502/503/504 and 429. 429s spike first, then 5xx climb as backend queueing increases.
- Request distribution: >70% of the requests came from a fleet of payment-worker processes (consistent with your note).
- Retry behavior: high concurrency + short fixed backoff (observed retry intervals ~200ms, no jitter) — this aligns with a typical retry storm.

Quick recommendations (technical):
1) Client changes (urgent):
   - Introduce exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=uniform(0, base))
   - Cap retries (max_retries=3) and cap overall inflight per-worker (<=8)
   - Respect Retry-After header and upstream 429 semantics
2) Server-side mitigations we're applying now (temporary):
   - Soft rate-limits per-api-key and per-IP for the next 30m
   - Queue pressure shedding for non-critical endpoints
   - Enable stricter circuit-breaker thresholds for your account PID=FP-3472

I've attached an anonymized excerpt of trace spans and error logs. We'll keep the soft limits in place while we validate the client fix.

—Vivek
SRE, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Devon Lee <devon@finpay.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 08:11:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Escalation: FinPay 5xx/429 spike — client config update

Thanks for the quick triage. We dug into our client config and found the following in our payment-worker image:

# snippet from client-config.txt (attached)
max_retries = 10
backoff_ms = 200
jitter = false

We pushed a hotfix at 08:40 UTC that was intended to improve throughput but inadvertently removed jitter and increased retry count. Rolling back + applying changes now:
- Set max_retries=3
- Switch to exponential backoff with jitter
- Add per-worker inflight cap to 6

We're deploying the fix to a canary pool and will report back once traffic stabilizes. Appreciate the mitigation steps on your side.

Devon Lee
Platform Engineer, FinPay
devon@finpay.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Asha Rao <asha@finpay.com>, Devon Lee <devon@finpay.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Incident closed: FinPay 429/5xx spike — next steps and postmortem

Team —

Thanks for the fast collaboration. Outcome: FinPay confirmed a bad client-side change (increased retries + removed jitter). Their rollback + our temporary soft rate-limits resolved the spike; error rates returned to baseline by ~12:30 UTC on 2026-02-22.

Action items:
- FinPay to roll the permanent client fix (max_retries=3, exponential backoff + jitter) to all workers (Devon).
- Redwood to publish a short runbook on guidance for client retry behaviour and default SDK config (Vivek + Platform Docs).
- Customer Success follow-up (Evelyn) to coordinate a scheduled postmortem call and discuss credits/SLAs.

I've opened a postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12567 and created the HubSpot case FP-3472. PagerDuty incident PD-9988 is closed.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
